implementer.summary:
W1-ATTACH is built on perf/attach. The branch contains the current perf/wave1 head (a26b6368, W1-EXEC), so merging it back has no conflicts.

Daemon (crates/zz-daemon/src/daemon/attach.rs plus daemon.rs):
- A fresh attach sends no second Snapshot and no overlay events for overlays that do not exist (ResyncScope::Attach). A requested Resync still sends everything.
- An update whose generation is already queued or already written is dropped (terminal_update_redundant). The written record is cleared exactly where the client wipes its viewports: when Attached is queued, on RequestFull, and on a full resync.
- Terminal frames are held until Attached is queued.
- A raw-terminal client that reports its size and cell size (new hello fact client-cell-v1) gets its panes resized before view streams start, so each pane's first Full is at the final size. Resync frames whose size is already out of date are skipped.
- Ready frames go out with writev in batches of up to 256 KiB. LocalStream now forwards write_vectored. The reliable lane stays FIFO, so kitty image chunks still go out before the frame that places them.

TUI (zz-tui):
- It drains up to 256 queued events and paints once. A snapshot repaints everything only when the frame structure changes.
- Nothing is painted before attach or into a pane that has no frame yet. Borders are written as runs. A paint that only puts the cursor back is skipped. Pane cards are cached.
- extended-keys and focus-events now arrive in the hello (server-option-v1:) instead of through two extra command connections.

This session:
- Removed the partial status-row repaint. The compat corpus reads raw pty bytes, and smoke/display-menu-action-queue broke on it. Changed status rows are written whole again, and the two zz-cli test patterns are back to their original form.
- Merged W1-EXEC. Two small conflicts in daemon.rs (the import list and a struct field), plus a type fix: ExecRequest.size keeps (cols, rows).
- Reran clippy, tests, all TUI fixtures, the full 254-scenario corpus and the gate, and updated the as-built notes in knowledge/designs/daemon-perf-rebuild.md.

Results:

review_parity.verdict:
Not ready to merge. There is one major regression, and it is a small fix. The lane's equal-generation dedup treats a queued PATCH as covering a Full at the same generation. So when a client has just dropped its viewport (after Attached, a failed patch, or a requested Resync), the Full it needs is thrown away and it gets a patch whose base it no longer has. After a RequestFull this leaves the pane blank or stale until the next Snapshot event, because zz-client core `full_pending` and the GUI's `full_requests_pending` hold back a second RequestFull. I proved this with three probe tests in an exported copy of 22455b48 (/tmp/zzprobe-attach, appended to the end of crates/zz-daemon/src/daemon/attach_tests.rs). All three fail on the lane defaults and pass with ZZ_PERF_ATTACH_DEDUP=0.

Everything else I tried held up:
- The lane's 11 attach_tests pass 30 times in a row, including under corpus load, with no hangs.
- cargo test -p zz-tui -p zz-client passes.
- 21 at-risk compat scenarios run against the pinned tmux were clean on the lane build and again with every lane knob off. They cover switch-client, alerts, aggressive-resize, resize-window, and these smoke scenarios: client-resized-context, copy-mode-refresh, display-popup-menu, display-popup-kitty, display-popup-to-pane, hooks-pane-focus-clients, pane-border-status, pane-border-lines, pane-border-indicators, refresh-status, display-menu-action-queue, display-menu-resize-lifecycle, control-notify, focus-follows-mouse, format-window-bigger, chooser-row-flags and client-exit-actions.
- All four attach paths release the terminal hold on error. Lock order is consistent: startup_config_causes, then snapshot_order, then the mailbox, then inner.
- Moving apply_terminal_resizes under the inner lock is safe, because TerminalSession::resize only writes a command slot.
- The hello values for the terminal options are read after the startup config is loaded, since wait_for_startup runs before register.
- Hook order at attach is now closer to tmux: window-layout-changed comes before client-session-changed and client-attached, as tmux's server_client_set_session calls recalculate_sizes first.
- The writev path is correct: std caps writev at IOV_MAX, advance_slices handles a short write, and a transport without write_vectored falls back safely.

One thing I need to own: my first probe build shared the lane's target directory, and cargo reused the same artifact hashes, so it overwrote the lane's zz_daemon test binary. I deleted those fingerprints and rebuilt from the lane source. `--list` now shows the lane's 11 attach_tests and no probe tests. The lane's source, git state and HEAD (22455b48) are untouched.

issues.where: crates/zz-daemon/src/daemon.rs terminal_update_redundant (used by enqueue_terminal_with, replace_terminal_with including its new pre-encode check), with OutboundMailbox::enqueue_attached, forget_delivered_terminal(s) and Shared::request_full in daemon/attach.rs
issues.issue: The pending-slot equality rule (`pending.current == current && (preview || !pending.preview)`) treats a queued patch as covering a Full at the same generation. The wipe points (Attached, RequestFull, requested Resync) clear delivered_terminals but leave queued patches in place, and those patches were built against the base the client is about to drop. So the Full the client needs is dropped and the stale patch is written instead. Before the lane, replace_terminal_with swapped a pending patch for the Full, and enqueue returned NeedsFull. After a RequestFull the client gets a patch with no base. zz-client core (used by the TUI, web and iOS) and the GUI then hold back the next RequestFull (`full_pending` / `full_requests_pending`), and later patches still match delivered, so the daemon never answers NeedsFull. The pane stays blank or stale until some Snapshot event clears the pending flag. The Attached case costs a round trip and a blank pane at best, and turns into the stuck case whenever the RequestFull that follows meets another queued patch at the latest generation. That is more likely over ssh or with a slow client, where the pending slot stays full longer. As built, this also contradicts the note's claim that clearing inside the enqueue lock means no attach epoch is needed.
issues.evidence:
Probe tests appended to /tmp/zzprobe-attach/crates/zz-daemon/src/daemon/attach_tests.rs (an export of 22455b48), run with an isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR.

Lane defaults:
- PROBE1 (Full 5 written, patch 5->6 queued, forget_delivered_terminal, replace_terminal Full 6): `replaced=false written=Patch %11`.
- PROBE2 (Full 5 written, hold, patch 5->6 queued, enqueue_attached, resync Full 6): `enqueue=Dropped written=Patch %12` after Attached.
- PROBE3 (live pane: attach-session, send-keys -l x, wait until a patch sits in the pending slot, then shared.request_full): `RequestFull answered with ["Patch %0"]`.

All three fail with the lane defaults and pass with ZZ_PERF_ATTACH_DEDUP=0.

On the client side:
- crates/zz-client/src/core.rs apply_patch: no viewport leads to request_full, which is held back while full_pending holds the pane. full_pending is cleared only by a Full, a Snapshot, or Attached.
- crates/zz/src/mux/client.rs request_full_viewport: held back by full_requests_pending, which is cleared only on SnapshotChanged or attach.
issues.fix: Record in PendingTerminal whether the queued frame is a Full (base is None). Only drop an incoming Full against the pending slot when the pending frame is a Full at that generation; against a pending patch, fall through to NeedsFull and replace it, as the code did before the lane. At the wipe points, also remove queued patches for the affected panes: remove_pending_terminal for patch entries in enqueue_attached's before_push, forget_delivered_terminals and forget_delivered_terminal. That way a patch built against the pre-wipe base can never follow the wipe. Add the three probe cases (pending patch plus RequestFull, pending patch across Attached, and the live-pane RequestFull) to daemon/attach_tests.rs.

issues.where: crates/zz-tui/src/app.rs, the InputOutcome::Resize arm (`unchanged` check near line 840) and the SIGWINCH path (`size == previous` near line 1002)
issues.issue: With ZZ_PERF_TUI_COALESCE on (the default), a resize to the same size sends ClientTerminalSize but repaints nothing. tmux redraws the whole client on every MSG_RESIZE, whether or not the size changed. So a same-size SIGWINCH, the usual way to recover a garbled outer terminal, no longer repaints under zz.
issues.evidence: compat/.cache/tmux-src/server-client.c:2455-2471: the MSG_RESIZE case calls recalculate_sizes, then server_client_clear_overlay or overlay_resize, then server_redraw_client(c), then notify_client("client-resized"), with no check that the size changed. In zz-tui app.rs, `let unchanged = *crate::COALESCE && size == model.size; ... if unchanged { continue; }` and `if *crate::COALESCE && size == previous { continue; }`. Both skip send_resizes_and_sync_browser and the forced paint.
issues.fix: On an unchanged size, skip send_resizes_and_sync_browser (no pane geometry changed) but still do renderer.invalidate() and paint(model, true), so the client is redrawn as tmux redraws it. Otherwise, list this as an accepted gap in the as-built notes.

issues.where: knowledge/designs/daemon-perf-rebuild.md, W1-ATTACH as-built, item 1 and item 2
issues.issue: The as-built notes overstate what clients do. Item 1 says every client resets overlays and viewports on Attached, but the GPUI desktop client keeps its own retained viewports across Attached; only zz-client core (TUI, web, iOS) wipes them. Item 2 says clearing the written record inside the lock that queues Attached means no epoch is needed, but that ignores patches already queued against the old base (see the major issue).
issues.evidence: crates/zz/src/mux/client.rs: finish_attach and the CoreEvent::Attached arm never clear self.viewports. Only clear_cross_host_state and forget_pane drop them. crates/zz-client/src/core.rs clears viewports in its handling of ProtocolMessage::Attached. See PROBE2 above for the queued patch.
issues.fix: Correct the two sentences when the major issue is fixed. State which clients wipe viewports on Attached, and that queued patches are dropped at every wipe point.

review_perf.verdict:
W1-ATTACH gains reproduce, and no regressions turned up in metrics the lane does not own. There are no blockers. Several pieces of avoidable work remain on the lane's own path, and two headline numbers in the report are misattributed or did not reproduce.

Method:
- I built a clean base at perf/wave1 a26b6368 in a scratch worktree. The zz-perf-int binary was older than that commit, so I did not use it.
- Interleaved gate runs of lane, base and lane with every knob off, at load 2.5-5 except where noted.
- xctrace Time Profiler (CPU-only samples) and lldb call counts against isolated daemons, using profiling-profile builds of the lane and the base.

Verified gains, lane vs base:
- attach.tty_total: 1915 vs 167.7-175.7 KB at p1, 5053-6239 vs 344.8 KB at p4.
- attach.conns: 4 -> 2. attach.wire_frames: 20 -> 6 at p1, 23 -> 9 at p4.
- attach.ttfc in full runs: 7.8-9.9 vs 14.7-25.2 ms at p1 (tmux 8.0-10.8), 8.0-8.9 vs 28.8-38.8 ms at p4.
- attach.cpu p1: 2.2-2.9 vs 3.0-4.5 ms. attach.instr p1: 16.0 vs 16.8 Minstr (-5%). Per-attach daemon CPU in the p4 loop: 2.84 vs 3.73 ms.
- TUI client CPU per attach: 12.0-12.4 ms vs 14.6-16.1 ms (tmux 11.0).
- The TUI's time from the Full arriving to the marker on the tty: 0.06-0.13 ms vs 3.2-5.5 ms.
- One Full encode per pane per attach (lldb: 4.75 vs 8.25 encode_viewport_into per p4 cycle).

No regressions:
- throughput.detached.ascii 247.5-252.3 vs 243.6-245.4 MB/s, which is 5.0-5.1x tmux.
- throughput.attached.ascii_ms 639-668 vs 653-661 ms.
- mem footprint and threads, idle, cli and chatty CPU are identical to base.
- The echo rows fail the same way on base (2.1-4.5x tmux).
- Rescored against the newest w1-5-exec-macbook-a26b6368.json: 0 regressed on every attach run. The full-gate run flagged chatty.steady and the echo p99 rows, but tmux moved the same way on a loaded host, so that is noise.

Fragile:
- attach.ttfc.p1 passes 14 ms only on a quiet machine. It passed in both full runs and one of three quick runs; the other two quick runs read 16.2 and 16.6 ms with tmux at 14.7-14.9.
- 60-65% of ttfc is CLI process start before the first daemon connect (5.7-9.9 ms). That belongs to W1-EXEC and W4-BINARY.

issues.issue: The first attach paint draws a placeholder status row (`[]` plus 178 spaces) and theme-coloured borders. Both are redrawn about 0.2 ms later when StatusChanged arrives, because the status is published after send_attached. The lane handed this to W2-CTRL, but send_attached and the TUI's attach paint are both in this lane's write zone.
issues.evidence: p1: the first paint is 247 of 1862 B (13%) and is fully overwritten. p4: the first paint is 1386 B of about 4.8-5.4 KB (26-29%), and the borders are redrawn in status style in the last 2040 B paint. Wire trace: Attached at 297.06, then StatusChanged at 297.27, then the Full at 297.38.
issues.fix: Have send_attached render and queue the client's StatusChanged in the same snapshot_order section, before or right after Attached, so one drained batch covers both. Or have the TUI hold the attach RepaintAll until the first StatusChanged or frame, with a short cap.

issues.where: crates/zz-daemon/src/daemon/attach.rs write_frames, and the daemon/client local stream setup
issues.issue: writev batching cannot reach the brief's ~2 write syscalls per attach. The macOS AF_UNIX send buffer is 8 KiB (net.local.stream.sendspace=8192), so each writev takes at most 8 KiB. The writer blocks and wakes once per 8 KiB, and the TUI reader wakes once per 8 KiB too.
issues.evidence: lldb counts per p4 attach+detach cycle: lane 8.75 writev + 1.75 write + 2 send = 12.5 socket writes; base 50 send + 4.25 write = 54. With about 100 KB per attach, 100 KB / 8 KB is about 12.5, which matches. The brief expected 29 -> ~2.
issues.fix: Set SO_SNDBUF on accepted local streams to at least MAX_BATCHED_WRITE_BYTES, and SO_RCVBUF on the client side. Then re-measure writes per attach and attach.cpu. The gain is not measured yet.

issues.where: daemon.rs attach_collect_event_hooks (apply_terminal_resizes, apply_view_streams, attach_view), the ResizeTerminal input path, and detach_client_state/unregister; zz-terminal TerminalSession::resize/with_slot
issues.issue: Every terminal command wakes the pane thread with its own wake write: 7 per pane per attach+detach. After presize, the TUI's ResizeTerminal re-sends the same geometry to each pane. TerminalSession::resize does not compare it with the current geometry, so each report costs another wake and another terminal-thread loop.
issues.evidence: lldb, per p4 cycle: 28 `write` calls from CommandSender::try_send. Each of these sends 4 per attach (one per pane): resize via apply_terminal_resizes, set_view_stream, attach_view, resize via input closure#5 (the redundant one), set_view_stream on detach, detach_view, release_view. poll in run_terminal is 193 us per attach (7.8% of daemon CPU).
issues.fix: Skip TerminalSession::resize when the geometry equals the last one applied. Wake only when a slot goes from empty to pending, so attach and detach each cost one wake per pane.

issues.where: daemon.rs handle_connection (`zz-client-writer-{client}` thread spawn) and exec.rs:682
issues.issue: A new writer thread is created and torn down for every TUI connection. write_outbound is in this lane's write zone. W1-EXEC reuses the connection handler threads, but not the writer thread.
issues.evidence: Time Profiler: pthread_create, _pthread_exit, _pthread_tsd_cleanup and _mi_thread_done take 83 us per p4 attach (3.4% of daemon CPU) and 21 us at p1 (1.2%). 39 distinct zz-client-writer-N threads appeared in 12 s of attach loop.
issues.fix: Run the outbound writer on a pooled or reused thread, as W1-EXEC's ConnectionThreads does for the handlers.

issues.issue: Every attach glob-matches the whole client environment against the update-environment patterns, even when nothing changed.
issues.evidence: 52-68 us per attach, 2.7-3.1% of daemon attach CPU (x-lane-a and x-lane-b profiles). GlobPattern::matches alone takes 2.5% self.
issues.fix: Compile the patterns once per option change, or skip the update when the client environment digest is unchanged since the last attach to that session.

issues.where: Remaining daemon work in the attach cycle that other lanes own (for the handoff list)
issues.issue: Most of the daemon CPU left in an attach+detach cycle sits outside this lane's changes. It still counts toward attach.cpu, which is at 1.4-1.7x tmux even though instructions are below tmux (16.0 vs 17.4 Minstr at p1).
issues.evidence:
CPU share per attach cycle, as p1 and p4:
- publish_snapshot_state: 448/458 us (26.7/18.6%). Of that, the status render on detach for the exiting TUI is 245/229 us (14.6/9.3%) and format_option_snapshot is 214/193 us (12.7/7.8%).
- run_terminal: 198/672 us, of which Frames::snapshot is 161/323 us.
- watch_terminal: 83/292 us. It calls tcgetpgrp and proc_pidinfo 16 times each per p4 cycle, 31/115 us (1.9/4.6%).
- write_outbound: 115/146 us.
issues.fix:
Record these in the plan's handoff list:
- Skip the status render for a detaching client (publish after detach_client_state excludes it). This could also land here, since it counts in attach.cpu.
- The option snapshot per publish: W1-FORMAT and W2-CTRL.
- The foreground lookup per wake: W1-PUBLISH and W4-DELIVER.
- Full viewport builds: W2-TERM and W4-ROWS.

issues.where: crates/zz-tui/src/tty.rs TerminalGuard setup (kitty graphics probe, probe_file_path) and the attach query burst
issues.issue: Every attach writes a kitty graphics probe that creates and removes a temp file (zz-tui-PID-probe.rgba). The probe and the terminal queries take 282 B of setup, even for TERM=xterm-256color. This predates the lane but is on the attach setup path it owns.
issues.evidence: Setup is 282 of 1862 B (15%) of the p1 tty_total in m-lane-a2.tty. It includes `\x1b_Gi=4294967294,...t=f,...` with a base64 temp path, plus `\x1b[c\x1b[>c\x1b[>q\x1b[?996n\x1b[16t`.
issues.fix: Probe kitty graphics only for terminals that can answer (the same terminal_supports list as pixel mouse), or cache the answer per TERM and terminal program. Leave file-transfer probing until an image actually needs it.
